concepts.preferred_label: Malignant Solitary Fibrous Tumor of the Pleura
aliases: Solitary Fibrous Tumor of the Pleura
support_spans: homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left
11 × 8.6 × 9.5 cm lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura
concepts.why: The presence of a large, lobulated solid mass arising from the pleura with mass effect on surrounding structures is unusual and points towards a malignant solitary fibrous tumor of the pleura.

support_spans: WBC 13.47 × 10^3/µL (85% neutrophils)
contradict_spans: anisocoria (right pupil 5 mm, left 3 mm)
concepts.why: The elevated white blood cell count with a high percentage of neutrophils could indicate a hematologic malignancy such as lymphoma, although the presence of anisocoria is not typical for this diagnosis.

support_spans: 11 × 8.6 × 9.5 cm lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura
contradict_spans: homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left
concepts.why: The large size and lobulated nature of the mass arising from the pleura could also suggest a pleural sarcoma, although the mass's effect on the trachea is not typical for this diagnosis.

support_spans: homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left
contradict_spans: anisocoria (right pupil 5 mm, left 3 mm)
concepts.why: The presence of a large mediastinal mass could indicate Ewing's sarcoma, a type of primitive neuroectodermal tumor, although anisocoria is not a typical finding for this diagnosis.

support_spans: homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left
contradict_spans: 11 × 8.6 × 9.5 cm lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura
concepts.why: The location and effect of the mass on the trachea could suggest thymic carcinoma, although the origin of the mass from the pleura is not typical for this diagnosis.

support_spans: homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left
11 × 8.6 × 9.5 cm lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura
concepts.why: The presence of a large mediastinal mass and a lobulated solid mass arising from the pleura suggests a possible diagnosis of lymphoma, which cannot be skipped due to its potential for aggressive behavior and need for prompt treatment.

support_spans: homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left
unquantified intermittent fever
concepts.why: The combination of a mediastinal mass and systemic symptoms such as fever suggests a possible diagnosis of sarcoidosis, which is a granulomatous disease that can affect multiple organs and requires consideration in the differential diagnosis.

support_spans: homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left
concepts.why: The presence of a mediastinal mass in the thoracic inlet region raises the possibility of thyroid cancer, which can metastasize to the mediastinum and cause compressive symptoms.

support_spans: unquantified intermittent fever
WBC 13.47 × 10^3/µL (85% neutrophils)
concepts.why: The presence of fever and an elevated white blood cell count suggests a possible infectious etiology, which must be considered in the differential diagnosis to guide appropriate antimicrobial therapy.

support_spans: homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left
11 × 8.6 × 9.5 cm lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura
concepts.why: A large mediastinal mass with lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms suggests lymphoma, which can cause respiratory failure and other symptoms described.

support_spans: homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left
contradict_spans: 11 × 8.6 × 9.5 cm lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura
concepts.why: A mediastinal mass in the anterior mediastinum can be a thymoma, but the described mass seems to be more posterior and larger than typical thymomas.

support_spans: homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left
11 × 8.6 × 9.5 cm lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura
concepts.why: A large mediastinal mass with a possible pleural origin can be a germ cell tumor, which can cause respiratory symptoms and have a varied presentation.

support_spans: homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left

concepts.why: A large and aggressive mediastinal mass with pleural involvement can be a sarcoma, which can cause respiratory symptoms and have a poor prognosis.
